title: performance: canary auto-detection and rollout guards for latency/throughput regressions
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: We've seen several rollouts where small changes triggered subtle latency regressions that only appeared at scale. This PR introduces an automated detection layer in the performance canary pipeline and rollout guards that prevent automated traffic shifts when regressions exceed configured thresholds.

Summary: Adds an auto-detection detector that consumes canary metrics (p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, error rate) and applies adaptive thresholds with hysteresis for upstream rollouts. The detector supports per-model and per-route baselines, sensitivity tuning, and KV-cache-aware checks. When a regression is detected the rollout guard will: 1) block automated traffic shifting to the new variant, 2) optionally trigger a rollback job, and 3) emit detailed diagnostics to the perf-canary dashboard and an incident Slack channel.

Design highlights: adaptive thresholds use exponentially-weighted moving averages of baseline metrics plus configurable multipliers; hysteresis prevents flapping by requiring sustained violations over a configurable window; KV-cache-aware checks discount transient cold-cache latency spikes by correlating cache-hit metrics. The rollout guard integrates with the existing canary controller and the traffic-shifting state machine; it exposes a small API to query current guard status and reasoning.

What changed: core detector implementation (pkg/perf/canary/detector.go), guard controller (pkg/perf/canary/guard_controller.go), metric adapters for KV cache (pkg/metrics/kv_adapter.go), a migration to persist model baselines (store/migrations/20260209_add_canary_baselines.sql), and end-to-end tests and canary job manifests. Also added dashboards and runbook links in docs.

Testing: unit tests for detector math and hysteresis (100% coverage for new package), integration tests using the perf-canary test harness with synthetic load and mocked KV-cache responses, and an end-to-end dry-run performed against staging that validated blocking behavior and Slack alerts.

Rollout plan: feature flagged by default (feature flag: perf_canary_autodetect_guards). After merge we'll enable on staging for two weeks, evaluate alerts and false-positive rate, then roll to canary-controlled models in prod behind a gradual ramp and human approval.

Checklist: 
- [x] Detector implementation + unit tests
- [x] Guard controller + integration tests
- [x] Metrics adapters and migration
- [x] Dashboard and runbook updates
- [x] Feature flag gating

Related: Linear ENG-4321, ENG-4419. See design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4321/canary-autodetect-design
